home.title: Alto Tevere
home.subtitle: Upper Tiber Watershed
home.tagline: A living territory, organized by ecological boundaries
home.section_place_body: The Alto Tevere watershed spans approximately 4,200 km² across Umbria and Tuscany. The Tiber rises on Monte Fumaiolo in Romagna and flows south through Apennine forests, upland pastures, and ancient towns before reaching Perugia.
home.section_life_body: This territory holds Apennine deciduous montane forests of beech above 900 m, turkey oak woodland in the hills, and a network of protected areas — Monti Sibillini, Monte Subasio, Monte Cucco — serving as corridors for Marsican brown bear, wolf, and golden eagle.
home.section_emergency_body: Lake Trasimeno — Italy's fourth largest lake — recorded a water level of −163 cm below the historical average (October 2025). Prolonged drought threatens the lake ecosystem and the communities that depend on it. The citizen movement 'Il lago al centro' is calling for coordinated action across Umbria and Tuscany.
